brief_notes:
Implementer notes (Claude Opus 5.5, the lead). Use them as context only; the judgment is yours.

Scope: `pose validate --carry` refreshes the canonical result by running the modules a change can affect since a comparable base and carrying the other checks with the head where they ran. Rounds 1–19 produced findings N1–N56. Each blocker was fixed and has a regression test that failed when its fix was mutated out. The spec's execution log lists them. Round 19 (rrn-fc6566de3c7eedf0) approved, but its conclusion was refused at preflight because decision D1 named no requirement. The spec now gives each decision a `- Basis:` line.

Change since round 19:
- The rule "refuse any base with an unavailable material binding" was removed. A clean record of this repository holds 77 specs whose material the engine cannot compute, recorded `unavailable` in every clean run, so that rule refused every real base.
- `material_clean` is the witness that a base validated its head. It requires one full predicate (status with forced fileMode, no hidden index entries, every submodule at its recorded commit, no nested submodules) at the pin, before any plan input is read, and at the end. It also requires unchanged reflogs of HEAD and of every submodule, and no cancellation.
- A run that is not clean records every binding unavailable.
Please check that removing the rule leaves no gap.

Draft format rules, enforced by the conclusion preflight:
- New findings use unprefixed IDs not used before (next free: N57). Round-prefixed IDs go only in `prior_findings`, with exactly id, status and evidence.
- Structural-delta mappings go inside the criterion that answers them, and only to decisions that declare a basis.
- A criterion scoped to a component cites evidence from that component only.

Sandbox limits: if building the CLI or creating scratch copies is read-only, run the focused Go tests (`go test ./internal/cli -run 'Carry|ChangedScope|Validate|Material|Cancellation'`, `go vet`) and cite the sealed canonical result for `validate` and `assess`, stating the limit, instead of stopping. Never `cd`; keep the checkout root as the Bash working directory.

Known follow-ups: F1 (end-to-end seal, verify and closeout over a carried record) and F2 (`--report` presents carried checks as executed). Account for R19-N55 (F2) and R19-N56 (F1), and report every remaining issue in this round.

Round 22 notes:
- Round 21 (rrn-20db50998dd91866) failed because `pose assess` commands ran inside the sealed checkout and rewrote `.pose/assessments/*` and `.pose/state/*`. Never run `pose assess` or any other writing command in the sealed checkout. If you cannot make a scratch copy, skip those tools and cite the sealed canonical result, stating the limit.
- Its draft found N57: the manual still described the removed unavailable-binding rule. All four manual copies now say an uncomputable binding does not refuse a base. N58/N59 restated F2/F1.
- The dogfood after round 21 carried five of six modules from a clean base with zero changed files; `pose-mcp` ran because of its high-criticality policy.
Account for R21-N57..R21-N59 and report every remaining issue.
